titleStmt.title: Shiji 史记 · 秦昭襄王五十六年: notes

div.interp: The fifty-sixth and last year of King Zhaoxiang of Qin, 251 BC.
我: the Table speaks from the standpoint of the state whose column it is, so "our army" is Yan's; the subject of 伐趙, "attacked Zhao", is likewise Yan.
The fourth year of King Xi of Yan, 251 BC; the text calls him "the present king" (今王).
四战之国: the Zhengyi: Zhao borders Yan to the east, Qin to the west, Han and Wei to the south and the Hu and Mo to the north, hence "at war on four sides".
The Suoyin: five men against one.

The Suoyin and the Zhengyi cite the Zhanguoce, which differs: Lian Po met Li Fu at Hao with two hundred thousand men, Yue Cheng met Qing Qin at Dai with fifty thousand, and the men of Yan were heavily defeated. The Zhanguoce writes the general's name 爰秦 (Suoyin) or 庆秦 (Zhengyi).
The Suoyin: Zhao wished to have Jiang Qu put in charge of making the peace; the Jijie: Yan made Jiang Qu its Chancellor.
The twelfth year of King Kaolie of Chu, 251 BC.
The fifteenth year of King Xiaocheng of Zhao, 251 BC.
尉文: the Suoyin: probably a place name, or else 尉 an office and 文 a name, the grant being the land that Wen had held; the Zhengyi: probably land in Weizhou.
The Hereditary House of Yan, above, has Yue Jian flee to Zhao.
The twenty-sixth year of King Anxi of Wei, 251 BC.
The twenty-second year of King Huanhui of Han, 251 BC.
槃散: the Jijie: also written 跚; the Suoyin: 散 is pronounced as 跚; the Zhengyi: 躄 means lame.
罢癃: the Suoyin: an ailment of the back, the waist bent and the back humped; Xu Guang: 癃 is an illness.
待: Xu Guang: one text reads 得, "winning".
颖脱而出: the Suoyin cites Zheng Xuan, 颖 is the ring; the whole awl would come through the bag, down to the ring of its handle.
The Suoyin cites Zheng Xuan: they all looked at him and smiled lightly, but could not yet discard him.
恶: the Zhengyi gives the pronunciation 烏故反, wu in the falling tone, "to hate".

The Suoyin: the victims of a covenant differ by rank, the Son of Heaven using an ox and a horse, the Lords a dog and a boar, Grand Masters and below a cock; here the blood of the covenant is named in general, hence "the blood of a cock, a dog and a horse".
The Suoyin: by the Rites of Zhou a pearl basin would be used.
录录: the Jijie and the Suoyin give the pronunciation lu; the Suoyin cites the Shuowen, "the look of one who follows along".

大吕: the Zhengyi: the great bell of the Zhou ancestral temple; the Suoyin: the Nine Tripods and the Great Lü are the treasured vessels of the state, so that Zhao was made weighty in the eyes of the world.
易德: the Zhengyi: gentlemen in their hour of danger and hardship easily feel gratitude.
Xu Guang: one text reads 是亲戚受城而以国许人, "for a kinsman to receive a Fortress and to promise the state to others".
右券: the Suoyin: if Yu Qing's proposal of a fief succeeds, he holds the right-hand half of the tally with which to claim the return of his favour.

251 BC. The Suoyin here says that the Table of the Six States and the Hereditary House both give the fourteenth year, unlike this; the Table as it stands gives the fifteenth, and the Suoyin on the Hereditary House cites it so.

The Jijie, Xu Guang: 尉文 is the name of a town; the Suoyin: 信平 is a title; the Hanshu's table has a Marquis Jie of Weiwen 尉文节侯, placed in Nan Commandery, so probably 尉 is an office and 文 a name, and the town that Wen had held in fief was given anew to Po, who was then styled Lord Xinping.
